answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the haven gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 113 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the prism ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the ridge review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
